fixed.how: The switch-off session read (store.session) now accepts only sessions with no account (user_id IS NULL), which is what the switch-off sign-in writes. So a switch-on session that has not passed MFA, is idle, or belongs to a disabled user no longer becomes a '*' session on a switch-off site. With the decided pairing (beta off, live on) this also ties every session to the site that made it, with no sessions.site column.

Migration 20261119_022 adds identities.seed_verifier_sha256 (the sha256 of the verifier the seed last wrote, never the verifier itself) and fills it for the seed's own identity. AccountStore.seed copies EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER only while sha256(verifier) still equals that mark. After a password change or reset on the switch-on site the identity belongs to the account and is never overwritten (logged account_seed_password_kept). The switch-off sign-in still reads the environment value directly. The recorded rule changed, so the README switch table and the seed docstring were updated.

fixed.how: Migrations 20261119_020 and _021 add site (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'beta', CHECK beta|live) to edge_bff.jobs and edge_bff.backtest_jobs. Store.submit, Store.claim and _promote carry and filter the site. BacktestStore(store, site) claims, reaps and prunes only its own site's jobs. The AI worker's claim is bound to the app's site (worker.claim, the same pattern as worker.access). Per-loop switches replace the single all-or-nothing switch: EDGE_AI_WORKER_ENABLED (unset means beta only; true on live is refused), EDGE_BACKTEST_LOOP_ENABLED, EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED, and EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED (the sender runs only with the switch on, so only on live). EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED=false still turns every loop off.

Duplicate of R2-7 plus R2-2, closed by the same fixes. config.validate also refuses the mixed pairings: EDGE_SITE=live without EDGE_MULTIUSER, and the beta with EDGE_MULTIUSER on outside EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local.

Duplicate of R2-7. The email outbox needs no site column: only the switch-on site (live) writes it and runs the sender. The hourly housekeeping runs in its own task, and an advisory try-lock on each purge stops two sites running the same purge at once.

Parts 1 and 2 are fixed as R2-7 and R2-2. EDGE_SITE (beta|live, default beta) is in place, and the live site masks every principal: principal.beta_only, live_view and Auth.site_view. On live nothing in the Monitor or admin tabs, no admin right from rights.py and no lab item is ever held, '*' included ('*' reads as every catalog flag that is not beta-only). allow_of never sends '*' from live. Auth.need answers 404 NOT_FOUND for those capabilities before the session is read, and /monitor and /c/<id> answer 404 too. MFA is still decided by the account's own grants, so user #1 needs MFA on live. Part 3 (the expand-then-contract order for 20261118_001 and 3c step 4) needs no code and is written into the notes for the records track. The pending test moved into apps/edge-bff/tests/ and was changed to the decided pairing (see notes).

What can be checked from one process: config.shared_key_marks() writes a 12-hex HMAC mark of EDGE_SESSION_SECRET, EDGE_CODE_SECRET and EDGE_MFA_KEY into every startup_done log line. The two services' lines then show whether they hold the same values, without logging any secret. The rule itself (edge-bff-live takes all three as ${{edge-bff.NAME}} references) is in the railway.ts comment block and in the notes for CONTRACT 16.

The secrets part is handled as in R2-8. The log-mode guard no longer accepts EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=dev, which is also the live site's Railway environment. Log mode with the switch on now needs EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local or an explicit EDGE_EMAIL_LOG_ALLOWED=true. That flag exists for a deliberate test on the live site before the Resend key, with no real person (the user asked on 2026-11-19 to test directly on weblive). While it is on, email_log_mode_allowed is logged at every start.

The start-up now runs as one attempt under a lock: readiness, seed, catalog names, seed plan, then the loops. The attempt runs in the lifespan, is retried every EDGE_POLL_SECONDS and on each /ready, and /ready answers 503 until it succeeds. No loop starts before that, the backtest loop included (store.ready reads no backtest table, so the reason for the old comment still holds). With the switch on, a failing seed fails the attempt. New log lines: startup_not_ready and startup_done.

The same start-up fix as R2-3. EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED, EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED and the new loop switches are parsed with switch_of, so a typo stops the start. email_sender_off is logged at error level whenever the switch is on and no sender runs.

The purges left the AI loop for worker.Housekeeping, a task of their own that also runs on live, where there is no AI loop. Each purge in store.PURGES (sessions, throttle, pending) now has its own transaction and its own try. It deletes at most 500 rows per batch (by key) and at most 20 batches per turn. A failed purge is retried after a backoff that doubles up to an hour, is logged as housekeeping_failed by error class, and is skipped while another instance holds its try-lock. purge_pending and throttle.purge take an optional limit and return the row count. BacktestLoop.run now runs prune (by site, batched), reap and claim each in its own try, and a failed prune backs off.

fixed.how: Migration 20261119_023 adds plain btree indexes on sessions(user_id), email_codes(user_id), admin_audit(actor_user_id), admin_audit(target_user_id), subscriptions(user_id, starts_at DESC) and user_capability_overrides(created_by_user_id). Its $verify$ block refuses any foreign key to users that lacks a leading non-partial index. Bounded EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) at the finder's sizes: purging 200 pending accounts went from 5830.7 ms to 27.4 ms; the resolve for an ended plan from 4.68 ms to 0.66 ms; the session cap from 8.96 ms to 0.13 ms; revoke_all from 9.27 ms to 0.24 ms. The site claims use the existing partial indexes (0.05 ms and 0.15 ms), so no index was added for site.

not_fixed.reason: No code change is needed; the refuters agree. The ordering rule is written into the notes for the records track (EXEC 'Production environment'): never pair a live edge-bff older than the 3b follow-up with 20261118_001, and hold 3c step 4 until every edge-bff sends the owner headers.

decisions_needed.context: The live website (edge-bff-live, app.edgefinance.id) is for users; the beta (edge-bff) is for the admin only, as the user decided ('beta hanya admin'). The decision does not say whether the admin's own account (user #1, edge-private, which holds every capability) may also sign in on the live site. As built, it can: it needs the authenticator code there too, and it sees the live site masked, with no Monitor, no admin pages, no point-in-time Flow and no lab items, much as a paying user would.
decisions_needed.options: A) Keep this: the admin can check the live site as a user sees it, with MFA. B) Refuse user #1's sign-in on the live site, so the admin works only on the beta.
decisions_needed.recommendation: A: it lets the admin check the live site after each push to live, and the mask plus MFA keeps the beta-only tools off the public site.

fixed.how: edge-bff now uses one rule, terminal_access.relayed (apps/edge-bff/app/terminal_access.py:303), for every terminal-api answer it relays: forward_terminal, relay_cut and PageFiles all go through it. A terminal-api 401, any 403 other than capability_required, a 400 about edge-bff's own owner headers, and every 5xx become 503 TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE in the contract shape, logged as terminal_refused with the upstream status and code. A 429 becomes 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details.limit terminal.<quota>, allowed, retry_after_s and the Retry-After header. A 400 about the request is answered 400 INVALID_INPUT, and a 404 is answered 404 NOT_FOUND; both carry terminal-api's code as details.reason. capability_required becomes CAPABILITY_REQUIRED with its display name. terminal-api's message text never reaches the page. On terminal-api, take() now raises quota_exceeded with quota, limit, window and retry_after_s, and sets the Retry-After header (wait_error). The wait comes from Store.frees_in: the seconds until the rolling window lets the refused request fit, read only on a refusal and never longer than the window. The service ceiling and the sign-in throttle send Retry-After too. In the Terminal page, live.ts now shows the contract's words instead of the code. M260 (public_data) was not applied; it needs the user's go.
fixed.tests: tests/test_cp0_terminal_relay.py: 2 now pass. New edge-bff tests/test_terminal_fix_round.py: a 16-case mapping table plus a route-level test (session kept, Retry-After, byte relay). New terminal-api tests/test_terminal_fix_round.py: the 429 fields, and frees_in on PostgreSQL 16. Changed because they locked the pass-through that CONTRACT section 3 forbids: test_terminal.py:84 and test_gateway_leaves_the_reference_names_to_terminal_api (now the contract shape with details.reason), and test_terminal_access.py test_a_cut_terminal_api_refuses_passes_through, renamed to ..._reaches_the_page_in_the_contract_shape.

fixed.how: PageFiles now answers a grant's 429 through the same rule: 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details and Retry-After, replacing <FAMILY>_QUOTA, and the QUOTA message is removed (apps/edge-bff/app/pages.py page_file). terminal-api sends the header and the structured fields (see R1-1).
fixed.tests: tests/test_c_p3a_probes.py -k retry_after: 2 now pass. Changed as the refuters said: test_radar.py:123-125 now expects LIMIT_REACHED with details and Retry-After, and its FakeHttp sends terminal-api's new fields.

fixed.how: Read side: terminal_access.capabilities now maps every value onto the wire. history_days above 36600 is sent as 36600. A value of 0 is sent as 0, which terminal-api now accepts as the empty window (entitlements MIN_HISTORY_DAYS); check() then refuses files, bundle, cut and history first with 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED terminal.history_days, so the page files keep working (the code refuter's correction). A ticker outside ^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$ is dropped and logged (count only). A quota of 0 is now 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED naming the limit instead of a 429, which was the refuters' 'other site'. Catalog side: new migration database/migrations/20261119_050_edge_bff_capability_domains.sql, not applied, added to tests/conftest.py, with a $verify$ block. It adds value_min, value_max and item_pattern to edge_bff.capabilities, and capability_value_check is replaced so it reads them after the shape check, with a hint that names the domain and gives an example. A new trigger, capabilities_domain_holds, refuses a domain change that a stored value would no longer fit. Domains set: terminal.history_days 1-36600; terminal.tickers 0-500 items matching ^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$, which also closes the case where a list of about 900 tickers gave 503 on every call; the four Terminal quotas 1-10^9. fixed.how: Option (a), using the task's reading of D3 = B ('no list of other tickers'). terminal-api now answers an owner whose plan lacks the dataset 'reference' with its own copy of each reference file (new apps/terminal-api/app/refcut.py). Which rows are kept is read from each file's own columns: a 'ticker' column keeps the plan's tickers; the broker list keeps its rows only when the plan holds 'broker'; any other file, today the stock lists, has no rows (fail closed). The copy is announced in the shape of a cut, '/api/terminal/v1/reference/<name>/cut?sha256=…'. It is served by GET /reference/{name}/cut and counted when served, with one audit row 'refcut/<name>/<sha>'. It is built from the published file after checking its sha256, uses deterministic gzip, and is cached. A file that cannot be filtered answers 503 reference_unavailable and is never served whole. A plan holding 'reference' gets the published file as before. ROUTE_ACCESS marks both reference routes 'filtered'. edge-bff now forwards reference/* without refusing it and relays the copy byte for byte (main.py TERMINAL_BYTES). The page draws as it does today. live.ts now tells a plan whose list holds no published ticker so (NO_TICKER) instead of crashing on tickers[0].

fixed.how: accounts.ORC_TEST_OWNER (Orc's TEST_OWNER_RE copied once, with a test that the two pattern texts are equal) and orc_reserved_owner (that rule plus 'default'). config.validate refuses it for EDGE_OWNER and for every EDGE_ADMIN_OWNERS entry, and the message names the forms with edge-private as the example. Per the refuters it does not use reserved_owner, so edge-private (the live owner) still validates.
fixed.tests: test_cp0_reserved_owner.py: the 4 re-check cases pass. Added: edge-private and 4 other keys validate, a reserved admin owner is refused, the pattern matches Orc's. Five existing tests used Orc-reserved admin-owner placeholders ('someone-else', 'golden-a'), which are now refused at start. They were renamed to 'another-owner' and 'another-a' in test_principal, test_manual_routes, test_releases and test_phase3a_fix_round.

fixed.how: Migration 20261119_011 adds mfa_totp.pending_nonce and pending_created_at (with CHECK mfa_totp_pending) and mfa_recovery_codes.pending. FlowStore.enroll decides under the row lock. With no confirmed enrolment it replaces the one candidate. With a confirmed one, only an MFA-passed session may start a new enrolment; that enrolment waits beside the confirmed one, whose authenticator and recovery codes keep working. use_step swaps it in on the first code of the new secret and deletes the old recovery codes then. Recovery codes of a waiting enrolment are never accepted.
New counter CODE_ADDRESS (keyed by the address, 20 a day). It is read and raised on every reset try, whether or not the address has an account. CODE_USER is kept for accounts.

SIGNIN_LOGIN is now keyed by (normalised login, client address). A reset proved by the email code clears the keys of the account's username and email for the resetting client, and (through R1-16) lifts the account cap. The SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT message carries {wait}, filled from details.retry_after_s (errors.message_of). The page fallbacks in edge-labels.js now say 'a few minutes'.
fixed.tests: test_cp1a f8 passes; test_fix_auth::test_tries_from_another_address_do_not_keep_the_owner_out, ::test_a_sign_in_limit_says_its_own_wait; test_auth_throttle.py keys moved to the new hash

fixed.how: Each throttle Limit has its own counter label inside the HMAC (scope, counter, key; a tuple key is written as a JSON list). REGISTER_HOUR and REGISTER_DAY share the 'register' label, so they stay one counter as the refuters required. The password change has its own PASSWORD_CHANGE counter. MFA_USER is keyed by the user id under its own label. No migration: the scope CHECK is unchanged, and existing counts restart once at deploy.

FlowStore.register returns keep_held when nothing was made and the browser's own cookie names a pending registration of the same address. The route then sets that cookie again. The refuters' qualifier is kept, so no other address is revealed.
Both 'taken' returns (the pre-check and the UniqueViolation branch) now raise the code's attempts; the code is consumed at 5.

New counter REGISTRATION_MAIL: one pending registration is mailed at most 3 times a day (its code, resends and sign-in restarts), keyed by its user id, checked in _issue_code. The registrations of others now use at most 6 of the address's 10 daily emails once its owner has registered. N4's record must be corrected to say this.
fixed.tests: test_cp1a f6 passes. test_auth_flows::test_resend_waits_60_seconds_and_sends_at_most_10_a_day was changed: one registration now stops at 3 emails, and the address's 10 a day is shown through an account's reset codes.

fixed.how: New constant accounts.EMAIL_MAX = 254, shared by checked_email, seed_identity and Login.login.

Migration 20261119_010 adds identities.sign_in_failures and sign_in_locked_until. AccountStore.sign_in_try decides and counts in one UPDATE before the password check, and the same statement runs for a login that names no account. The 100th consecutive failure (both logins, every address) starts a 24 h lock, answered as a wrong password (OWASP: the same answer). After the lock the count restarts at 90, as the MFA counts do. A success (in create_session), a reset or a change clears it, and scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py now also clears the password count of the account it unlocks. This applies with the switch on only (decision 2).

The account's users row is now the lock for credential writes (AccountStore.lock_account). create_session takes it and checks the request's proof: `proved` compare-and-sets the verifier the sign-in proved (and stores the rehash), `replaces` requires the MFA verify's pending session to be live and revokes it in the same transaction. FlowStore.change takes the lock and checks that the changing session is live (else 401 UNAUTHENTICATED) and that the proved verifier is still the account's (else 400 CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID). revoke_all takes the lock; reset already did.
_may_send's 60-second gap reads only code purposes (CODE_PURPOSES, the purposes of email_codes), so a notification email no longer holds a code back.
fixed.tests: test_r2_race hold_back (both) pass; test_fix_auth checks CODE_PURPOSES against the email_codes CHECK

fixed.how: use_step(user_id, CheckedStep(nonce, step)) confirms only the enrolment whose nonce was checked (confirmed, candidate or waiting). Otherwise the try counts as a failure. The 2-argument shape the committed test patches is kept.

FlowStore.mfa_try decides (including the restart after a lock), checks and counts in one transaction under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE of the enrolment. The recovery-code use happens inside that transaction.

Migration 20261119_012 adds edge_bff.purge_email_outbox(). It is SECURITY DEFINER with a fixed search_path, and only edge_bff_runtime may execute it. It deletes sent, failed, expired or suppressed rows older than 24 h of addresses with no users row, at most 10 000 per call. Store.cleanup_sessions runs it in a transaction of its own after the pending purge. The runtime still holds no DELETE on the outbox, so 20261116_003's verify block, test_principal:210 and EXACT_GRANTS stay true. Rows of addresses that have an account are kept (decision 1).

errors.UnexpectedErrors, added last so it is the outermost middleware. It answers 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE in the contract's shape, logs request_failed with method, path, class and SQLSTATE only, and never re-raises.

security.COST is now (16384, 8, 5) and the verifier names its cost: scrypt$n=16384,r=8,p=5$salt$hash. Only the costs in COSTS are read. An old (p=1) verifier is checked and then padded with a p=4 derivation, so every check costs the same (M478 N1 holds). A switch-on sign-in with an old verifier stores the new one inside its create_session transaction. EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER may be in either form. Migration 20261119_010 widens the identities_password CHECK to both forms. Measured here: 52 ms per derivation at p=1, 235 ms at p=5.
fixed.tests: test_fix_auth: new verifiers, equal cost, rehash at sign-in, configured verifier of either form

fixed.how: Migration 20261119_012 adds two indexes: email_outbox_to_email_created (to_email, created_at) and email_outbox_unsent (next_at) WHERE status IN ('pending','sending'). With them, no Seq Scan of the outbox remains on the four hot statements at 20k rows. The purge is under R2-24.

New passwords.PasswordWork: 4 threads of its own, and at most 16 requests in password work at once (sign-in, register, reset, change). The next request is answered 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After 5 before any try is counted. The Pwned Passwords call also runs there. The default executor stays free for database calls.

not_fixed.reason: Enforcing SIGNIN_IP (30 failed sign-ins per client address per 15 min) needs the Railway client-address probe first (CONTRACT 4 'Client IP', a Phase 0 runbook step that requires a Railway call). If Railway's edge does not add the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop, every client shares one address, and an enforced per-address limit locks everyone out. The refuters rejected a global cap in the meantime. The bounded password pool already stops a flood from stalling signed-in users.

One row per made-up login, purged hourly by a full scan. A batched purge in its own transaction belongs with R2-33 (the cleanup that stops the run queue, another track). A window_start index waits for that design and its measurement (AGENTS.md: no speculative index).
terminal-api has no Exception handler either. It needs the same outermost middleware before 3c's per-owner writes, but apps/terminal-api is the terminal track's code. Noted in fix_round/auth.md.

A 'Forgot password?' within a live code's life still replaces the code, and the address's 10 emails a day are still shared with strangers. Changing this changes CONTRACT 1 ('a new code consumes the old one'); see decision D3.

Starting a re-enrolment does not require a fresh code. The re-check's own f3 test starts a re-enrolment with no body from an MFA-passed session and expects 200. The waiting enrolment (built) closes the takeover path; the stolen-verified-cookie case is decision D4.

decisions_needed.context: Every email EDGE sends leaves a row in the database's email outbox: the recipient's address, the kind of email (a code, 'password changed', 'account exists'), when it was sent and Resend's id. The email's text is removed once it is sent. Until now nothing ever deleted these rows. This branch deletes them 24 h after they were made, but only for addresses that have no EDGE account (registrations that were never verified, which CONTRACT 4 already deletes after 24 h, or addresses never registered). Rows of addresses that do have an account are kept for ever. With accounts switched on, each account adds a row for every code, reset and password change (up to 10 a day). EDGE reads only the last 24 h (the 60-second and daily limits), and Resend's idempotency key lasts 24 h, so nothing needs an older row. Used email codes and Resend webhook events also pile up. The Phase 6 Privacy text must state a retention period.
decisions_needed.options: A: delete sent, failed, expired and suppressed rows of every address after 30 days, and the same for used codes and webhook events. B: delete after 24 h. C: keep them while the account exists and delete them with it. D: another period you name.
decisions_needed.recommendation: A. It is one migration that replaces edge_bff.purge_email_outbox().

decisions_needed.context: Sign-in to the beta website (accounts switched off, admin only, login EDGE_LOGIN) is now limited per login and per client address: 10 wrong passwords per 15 minutes from one address. A stranger can no longer keep the admin out just by typing the login. The new per-account cap (at most 100 wrong passwords in a row, the NIST SP 800-63B-4 rule) is built only with accounts switched on, where 'Forgot password?' is the way back. The beta has no reset. If the cap applied there, anyone who sent 100 wrong passwords would lock the admin out for 24 h, again and again, and only the operator script could unlock it. Without the cap, someone with many client addresses can guess the beta admin's password at up to about 960 tries a day per address, and the beta has no second sign-in step with accounts off.
decisions_needed.options: A: no cap on the beta (as built), with a long random admin password. B: the same 100-cap with its 24 h lock on the beta; the way back is scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py or waiting. C: open the beta website only to known client addresses (a Railway change).
decisions_needed.recommendation: A now. Add C if the beta's address becomes widely known.

decisions_needed.context: 'Forgot password?' emails a new 6-digit code, and each new code cancels the one before (CONTRACT 1). An address gets at most 10 EDGE emails a day. Anyone who knows an account's email address can press 'Forgot password?' for it. Every minute that cancels the owner's code (the owner gets the new code too, so this alone is a nuisance). After 10 presses in a day, the owner's own 'Forgot password?' sends nothing until the next day. This branch stopped notification emails from holding codes back (R2-10) and limited registrations by others (R1-13), but this budget is still shared by design.
decisions_needed.options: A: keep as is. The owner may wait up to a day after such an attack, but the sign-in limit and the account cap no longer lock them out. B: a 'Forgot password?' within a live code's 5 minutes sends nothing and keeps that code (fewer emails; someone who lost the email waits 5 minutes). C: count resets per address and client address, so a stranger's presses do not use the owner's budget (but then many client addresses could flood one mailbox).

decisions_needed.context: An admin who changes phone sets up a new authenticator from a session that has already passed the second sign-in step. This branch keeps the old authenticator working until the new one is proved by its first code, so a password alone can no longer take over the second step (R1-7). But someone who steals an admin's already-verified session cookie can still start and confirm an authenticator of their own, because starting one asks for no fresh code. OWASP's MFA cheat sheet asks for the current factor before it is changed.
decisions_needed.options: A: the request that starts a new authenticator must carry a code from the current one (or a recovery code); the set-up screen gets a code field. B: the session must have passed the second step in the last 10 minutes, otherwise it verifies again first. C: keep as built.
decisions_needed.recommendation: B. No page change, and it fits the re-check's own test, which starts a re-enrolment right after MFA.

decisions_needed.context: Passwords are stored as scrypt verifiers. Following the fix round's brief (R2-29), this branch raises the cost from N=2^14, r=8, p=1 to OWASP's minimum equivalent at 16 MiB, N=2^14, r=8, p=5. Measured on this machine: 52 ms per derivation at p=1, 235 ms at p=5. A sign-in with accounts switched on (the live website) derives 4 times (one for the account and 3 padding, so the time reveals nothing), which is about 0.9 s of CPU per sign-in. At most 4 derivations run at once on the new password pool, so a burst of sign-ins waits its turn. Old verifiers keep working and are replaced at each account's next sign-in. The edge-bff test suite took about 19 min instead of 12.5 min on this shared machine.
decisions_needed.options: A: keep p=5 (as built). B: N=2^15, r=8, p=3 (32 MiB, about the same CPU). C: go back to p=1 and record it as accepted in CONTRACT 4 (5 times weaker against a database leak).

contract_changes: Section 1, identities: the verifier is scrypt$<salt>$<hash> (old, p=1) or scrypt$n=..,r=..,p=..$<salt>$<hash>; new columns sign_in_failures and sign_in_locked_until.

Section 4 Throttle: sign-in is limited to 10 failures per login and client address per 15 min (was per login). Section 4 Registration rules: verifiers use scrypt N=2^14, r=8, p=5 and name their cost; an old verifier is replaced at the next sign-in (decision D5 confirms the cost).
Section 4 Sessions: reset, change, sign-out everywhere, sign-in and MFA verify serialise on the account's users row; a sign-in, change or verify whose proof no longer holds is refused.
Section 4 Admin MFA: a confirmed enrolment is replaced only by an MFA-passed session, and only once a code of the new authenticator proves it; until then the new one waits beside it.

Deploy order and rollback:

- Once a switch-on sign-in has rehashed a verifier, an older edge-bff cannot read it. Ship this version to every website that has the switch on before any rehash happens, and do not roll back below it without replacing those verifiers (stated in 010's rollback comment).
